title: Part II, Book IV, Chapter II

verses.t: The God declares the deities' generations, like Usana, proclaiming lofty wisdom. With brilliant kin far-ruling, sanctifying, the wild boar, singing with his foot, advances.
The swans, the Vrishagnas from anear us, restless, have brought their clamour to our dwelling-- Friends come to Pavamana, meet for praises-and sound in concert their resistless music.
He takes the swiftness of the great Far strider: cows low as, 'twere to him who sports at pleasure. He with the sharpened horns brings forth abundance: the silvery shines by night, by day the golden.
Like cars that thunder on their way, like coursers eager for renown, Have Soma drops flowed forth for wealth.
Forth have they rushed from holding hands, like chariots that are urged to speed, Like joyful songs of singing-men.
The Somas deck themselves with milk as kings are graced with eulogies, And, with seven priests, the sacrifice.
Pressed for the gladdening draught the drops flow forth abundantly with song, Flow with the stream of savoury juice.
Winning Vivasvan's glory and speeding the light of Dawn, the suns, Pass through the openings of the cloth.
The singing-men of ancient time open the doors of sacred songs-- The men who bring the mighty One.
In close society have come the priests, the sevenfold brotherhood, Filling the station of the One.
He makes us kin with Gods, he joins the Sun, for seeing, with mine eye; I milk the Sage's offspring forth.
The Sun beholdeth with his eye the heaven's dear quarter which the priests Have set within the sacred cell.
Forth on their way the glorious drops have flowed for maintenance of Law, Knowing what suits this worshipper.
Down in the mighty waters sinks the stream of Meath, most excellent, Oblation best of all in worth.
About the holy place the Steer, true, guileless, noblest, hath sent forth, Continuous voices in the wood.
When the Sage, purging manly deeds and lofty wisdom flows, around,
When purified, he sits enthroned as King over the warring clans. What time the sages speed him on.
Most dear, gold-coloured, in the fleece he sinks, and settles in the wood: The singer is besieged with song.
He goes to Indra, Vayu, and the Asvins with the rapturous joy, To whomsoe'er his power delights.
The waves of pleasant Soma flow to Bhaga, Mitra, Varuna, Well knowing, through his mighty powers.
Gain for us, O ye Heaven and Earth, riches of Meath to win us strength: Gain for us treasures and renown.
We choose to-day that chariot-steed of thine, the strong, that brings us bliss, The guardian, the desire of all;
The excellent, the gladdener, the Sage with heart that understands. The guardian, the desire of all;
Who for ourselves, O thou most wise, is wealth and fair intelligence, The guardian, the desire of all.
Agni Vaisvanara, born in course of Order, the messenger of earth, the head of heaven, The Sage, the Sovran, guest of men, our vessel fit for their mouth, the Gods have generated.
To thee, immortal! when to life thou springest all the Gods sing for joy as to their infant. They by thy mental powers were made immortal, Vaisvdnara when thou shonest from thy parents.
Him have they praised, mid-point of sacrifices, great cistern of libations, seat of riches. Vaisvanara, conveyer of oblations, ensign of worship, have the Gods engendered.
Sing forth unto your Varuna and Mitra with a song inspired: They, mighty Lords, are lofty law.
Full springs of fatness, sovran Kings, Mitra and Varuna, the twain, Gods glorified among the Gods,
So help ye us to riches, great celestial and terrestrial wealth! Vast is your sway among the Gods.
O Indra marvellously bright, come, these libations long for thee, Thus by firie fingers purified!
Urged by the holy singer, sped by song, come nigb, O Indra, to The sacrificing suppliant's pravers!
Approach, O Indra, basting thee, Lord of bay horses, to our prayers: In our libation t ake delight!
Glorify him who compasses all forests with his glowing Dame, And leaves them blackened by his tongue.
He who gains Indra's grace by fire enkindled, finds as easy way Over the floods to splendid wealth.
Give us, ye twain, swift steeds to bring Indra and Agni, and bestow Abundant food with wealth on us.

Indu hath started forth for Indra's settled place, and slights not,. as a friend, the promise of his friend. Soma comes onward like a youth with youthful maids, and gains the beaker by a course of hundred paths.

Your hymns of pleasant sound, praiseworthy, fond of lauds, have come into the hall enclosed for sacrifice. Singers have hymned the golden-coloured as he sports, and milchkine have come near to meet him with their milk,

O Soma, Indu, while they cleanse thee, with thy wave pour orb us plentiful accumulated food, Which, ceaseless, thrice a day shall yield us hero power enriched. with store of nourishment, and strength, and meath.
No one by deed attains to him who works and strengthensevermore: No, not by sacrifice, to Indra praised of all, resistless, daring, bold in might;
The powerful conqueror, invincible in war, him at whose birth the mighty ones, The kine who spread afar, sent their loud voices out, heavens, earths sent their loud voices out.
Sit down, O friends, and sing aloud to him who purifies himself: Deck him for glory, like a child, with holy rites
Loose him who bringeth household wealth, even as a calf with. mother kine, Him who bath double strength, strong, god-delighting juice!
Purify him who gives us power, most blissful one, that he may be A banquet for the troop, Mitra, and Varuna!
The Strong hath flowed forth in a thousand streams, flowed through the filter and the sheep's long wool.
With ceaseless genial flow the Strong hath run, purified by the waters, blent with milk.
Pressed out with stones, directed by the men, go forth, O Soma, into Indra's throat!
The Soma juices which have been expressed afar or near at hand, Or there on Saryanavan's bank,
Those pressed among Arjikas, pressed among the active, in, men's homes, Or pressed among the Fivefold Tribes--
May these celestial drops, expressed, pour forth upon us, as they flow, Rain from the heavens and hero strength!
May Vatsa draw thy mind away even from thy loftiest dwelling-place! Agni, I yearn for thee with song.
Thou art alike in many a place: through all the regions thou art Lord. In fray and fight we call on thee.

When we are seeking spoil we call Agni to help us in the strife, Giver of wordrous gifts in war. 1, O Indra, bring great strength to us, bring valour, Śatakratu, thou most active, bring A hero conquering in war!
For, gracious Satakratu, thou hast ever been a mother and a sire to us, So now for bliss we pray to thee.
To thee, strong! much-invoked! who showest forth thy strength, made very mighty! do I speak: So grant thou us heroic power!
Stone-Darting Indra, wonderous God, what wealth thou hast not given me here, That bounty, treasure-finder! bring, filling full both thy hands, to us!
Bring what thou deemest worth the wish, O Indra that which is in heavem! So may we know thee as thou art a giver boundless in thy gifts!
Thy lofty spirit famed in all the regions as appeasable,-- With this thou rendest even things firm, Stone-darter! so to win thee strength.
